back: If y = f(x) varies with time, dy/dt = f'(x) dx/dt. Always link quantities through a relation first, then differentiate.
f is increasing on I if f'(x) ≥ 0 for all x in I (strictly increasing if > 0). Decreasing if f'(x) ≤ 0.
f'(c) = 0 and f' changes from + to − at c ⇒ c is a local maximum of f.
f'(c) = 0 and f' changes from − to + at c ⇒ c is a local minimum of f.
If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) < 0 ⇒ local maximum; f''(c) > 0 ⇒ local minimum.
If f''(c) = 0 alone, use the sign chart of f' to decide; no sign change ⇒ point of inflexion, not an extremum.
Evaluate f at all critical points inside [a,b] AND at the endpoints x = a, x = b; pick largest/smallest.
At (x₀, y₀) on y = f(x): y − y₀ = f'(x₀)(x − x₀).
Slope of normal = −1/f'(x₀) when f'(x₀) ≠ 0. Equation: y − y₀ = (−1/f'(x₀))(x − x₀).
Tangents parallel to a given line have slope m: f'(x₀) = m. Perpendicular: f'(x₀)·m = −1.
A horizontal tangent occurs where f'(x₀) = 0 (slope zero).
f(x + Δx) ≈ f(x) + f'(x) Δx. Use when Δx is small; the new value is the old plus the tangent's change.
dy = f'(x) dx; absolute error Δy, relative error Δy/y, percentage error 100·Δy/y.
Express everything in a single variable using the constraint, find critical points, and check the admissible range and the value at endpoints.
If f continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), ∃ c with f'(c) = (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a).
A point where f'' changes sign (concavity changes); solve f''(x) = 0 and verify the sign change.
If f(a) = f(b), then between them lies a point with f' = 0; useful for locating extrema.
Typical mistake: differentiating the numbers instead of the variables. Keep the variables symbolic until the end.
Volume of box: V = x(a − 2x)(b − 2x). Surface area of cylinder: S = 2πrh + 2πr². Use these templates.
For (1 + x)^n with small x, ≈ 1 + n x. A 1% change in x gives an n% change approximately.
